+++ Traditionally the elite warriors known as the Hearthguards accompany the Warlord as his personal bodyguards, however their duties do not end there. Hearthguards who are not in the direct service of the Warlord take the position of platoon "captains", leading troops directly into battle. Only when a Hearthguard has proven to be a charismatic leader, a resourceful strategist, and a skilled warrior, he can be considered to be part of the Warlord's personal guard in the future.

The Hearthguards go into battle accompanied by an retinue of warriors selected from among the most skilled and trusted veterans, as they carry valuable weapons known as "heirloom weapons." These weapons are evidence of the maximum skill of the squat artificers, surpassing in every aspect their more common equivalents, and many of them have been in service of the squat noble families for centuries and some even millennia. +++

This is a Squat Hearthguard unit designed for NetEpic Armageddon, in specific for the Grindel Sronghold army list that you can find here: https://tacticalwargames.net/taccmd/viewtopic.php?f=134&t=33281&sid=422418b4bea515739e1aef8d862588e5

I designed 3 Hearthguard models, all equiped with a plasma and volkite pistols. Also i included a banner-bearer squat.

You can complete the unit using the warriors models that i already uploaded.

+++ The individuals known as Grand Warlords are rarely seen, appearing only in the largest of battles where their great tactical skill and commanding presence are necessary to control a vast army of countless soldiers and monstrous war engines. The title itself is temporary, lasting for the duration of the campaign and generally being awarded to a warlord who stands out above the rest due to his martial achievements, although it is also possible that the Stronghold Lord himself is the one who wears the powerful Exo-armor distinctive of the Great Warlord. However, although it grants great honor and renown, it is a position that implies tremendous responsibility that not everyone is willing to assume or able to fulfill, and for a Great Warlord defeat in battle means ruin and contempt for his clan for generations.

The Living Ancestors are the oldest individuals in Squat society, who form the basis of their religion. For all intents and purposes, the Living Ancestors have abandoned their previous life and identity and are now regarded as vessels of the spirits of the deceased, who observe and judge all the actions of the Squats. In battle they provide wisdom and advice for leaders, and physical support for warriors, because their long life (or perhaps also due to the influence of spirits) has allowed them to develop psychic powers which focus on defense and healing, but they are not completely incapable of attacking if they are forced to do so, although with much disgust. +++


These are a Epic scale Squat Grand Warlord and a Living Ancestor for the Grindel Sronghold army list that you can find here: https://tacticalwargames.net/taccmd/viewtopic.php?f=134&t=33281&sid=422418b4bea515739e1aef8d862588e5

They are considered characters, which means that they do not form individual units but must join an existing one. As you can see in the photos, I attached them to a Warlord unit, because I think it makes sense, but they are not restricted to this unit only.

On the battlefield he is accompanied by a unit of elite warriors knows as Hearthguard, each one drawn from the Lord's loyal retainers, who formed an aristocratic class in Squat Strongholds. +++

The list does not consider the classic Squats exosuits, which gave me some creative freedom and I decided that both the warlord and his hearthguard would be equipped with power armor, for which I used (again) the fantastic models designed by Toftylicious. This also opens the possibility of creating an Epic scale army of squat marines in the distant (grimdark) future.

I have designed two warlord models, one with a thunder hammer and one with a power axe; two hearthguard models, although the difference is almost imperceptible; and a banner-bearing hearthguard.

About the very small supports, i placed each one by hand so probably many are redundant or totally unnecesary for the model size, but overall they gave good results on printing.

A slightly unhinged reworking of Moonjammy's excellent design, optimised for _crazy_ printing!

A new concept for creating simple, stackable supports for Epic scale infantry! Create blocks of infantry in any arbitrary width and height simply by copying strips in Lychee and moving them vertically, no additional fine-tuning required!

**ARE STACKABLE SUPPORTS RIGHT FOR ME?**

Stackable supports are resin-inefficient compared with printing a single squad flat on the build plate, but time and clean-up efficient, allowing you to print large numbers of troops in a single print without having to get up to scrape them off the build plate, clean up, and restart your print every hour!

Stackable supports also allow you to make effective use of empty space on your build plate when printing larger vehicles or 28mm scale models. Just create a stack as tall as your other models!

**UH OH, THIS LOOKS COMPLICATED! IS REMOVING THE SUPPORTS HARD?**

De-supporting these is easy and risk free!
The heavy supports only make contact with the pseudo-rafts so you can yank them off without any worries. Then just use a knife tip or tweezer to pick off the remaining supports on the individual models.

**I THINK MARK 2s ARE STUPID! ARE YOU GOING TO SUPPORT OTHER TYPES OF INFANTRY?**

Probably! Eventually! But until I get round to it, feel free to try this style of supporting on your own models 😁

*Like what I'm doing? [Buy me a cup of resin!](https://ko-fi.com/lstar)* 😁

The Empire of Sentient Man cannot reclaim constant victories over space elves who constantly terrorize human realms. But this doesn’t mean they cannot beat the foe in local skirmishes. Besides many elven hover vehicles with controversial fusion of organic and greebled shaped apparatus, defenders of man had found many weapons considered by logics of military art. This cobbled-together flying piece of scrap metal looks as if it should fall apart under a gentle breeze. And yet, it barrels through the air with wild abandon; bullets, bombs and stranger projectiles flying from it in all directions. A mighty flying fortress, this super-scrap bomber all but ignores incoming fire as it passes harmlessly through open superstructure, or as it blasts away rusty plating that was all but falling off anyway, leaving critical structures safe below layers of bolted on scrap metal.

This 67 piece multi-part kit comes with a huge range of options. It can be built with two wing profiles, alternative hulls with differing tailfins, and a range of options for turrets and bombs, many of which can be mirrored for additional variety / symmetry. It includes monstrous 'bouncing bombs' for some truly 'wild' bombing runs!

The kit is designed to be scaled to 8mm scale model games, such as plane warfare games, or those featuring legions of models fighting. It could also be used in 6mm games where Epic Marines fight in Space, a real armageddon level battle. Compatable with ork style armies, it would be a great proxy for a mega bommber or landa. It is sufficiently detailed that an ambitious hobbyist could print it at 400% scale to create a huge center piece model or terrain for 32mm games set in grim dark universes. This would of course require additional cuts to the model!

I am a hobbyist 3D modeller - not a professional 3D designed. However, this project has taken many, many hours of development, test printing and correction. It is my first 'paid for' model, a reflection of the time it took to create. Almost all my other models are currently available for free, so please do look through those if you are interested in further supporting me and my hobby.

I also welcome feedback and will look to develop this model with improvments and additional options in future.

"'Ere We Go, 'Ere We Go, 'Ere We Go!"
— Common Ork chant heard during a Greenskin WAAAGH!
The Orks, also called Greenskins, are a savage, warlike, green-skinned race of humanoids who are spread all across the Milky Way Galaxy. They share many features with Warhammer Fantasy Orcs (and were initially called "Space Orcs" to distinguish them). They are seen by their enemies (pretty much everyone else in the universe) as savage, warlike, and crude, but they are the most successful species in the whole galaxy, outnumbering possibly every other intelligent race, even Mankind (with the very plausible exception of the Tyranids).

Greenskins are one of the most dangerous alien races to plague the galaxy. Numerous beyond belief and driven always to fight and conquer, the Orks threaten every single intelligent species of the galaxy. Orks are possibly the most warlike aliens in the 41st Millennium, and their number is beyond counting. Amid constant, seething tides of war and bloodshed, burgeoning Ork stellar empires rise and fall. Mercifully most are short-lived, soon destroying themselves in a maelstrom of violence and internecine conflict, but should the Orks ever truly unify, they would crush all opposition.

The Orks' unquenchable thirst for battle has always proved their downfall: historically, the Ork tribes have spent much of their time fighting amongst themselves, waging brutal wars with only the strongest surviving. On occasion, an Ork leader will emerge who is mighty enough to defeat his rivals and unite the warring tribes. His success draws other tribes to him, and soon a great WAAAGH! is underway -- partly a migration, partly a holy war that can exterminate the populations of entire star systems. When the Orks are on the rampage, the galaxy trembles, and in these dark days of the End Time, there are more WAAAGH!s rising than ever before recorded.

There have been woolly, tusked Squiggoths seen on battlefields, but the most common appears similar to a dinosaur. It commonly has a howdah on its back, where boyz ride into battle, shooting mounted guns, such as the Supa-lobba as they go. To protect their "ride", Orks usually add armour plating.

As with all Greenskin organisms, the Magos Biologis of the Adeptus Mechanicus have identified Squiggoth's as fungal lifeforms, though they are fairly rare and can only be grown by the specialist breeder Pigdok of the Snakebites Clan. The size of the Squiggoth is determined by the effectiveness of the feed-formula the breeder gives his creature. Less-effective formulas may result in puny Squiggoths while high-quality formulas will see them keep growing and growing.

Squiggoths themselves vary in size and shape, but there are two primary subspecies:

Big Squiggoths are the smaller but more common breed of Squiggoths, either young or whose breeding and feed were less effective and have stunted growth. They most often travel in packs.
Gargantuan Squiggoths are monsterous creatures the size of a small Imperial Titan, bred from the finest secret feed-formulas of the Snake Bites Clan. They are sometimes the favored steeds of powerful Ork Warbosses.

***THIS IS A WORK IN PROGRESS***

Tiny troops which are perfect for giving your games of epic conflict a sense of epic scale. And what can be more perfect than the golden perfect winged assault cherubs?

Building on the foundation that Moonjam left us, I've remodeled and rebuilt most of the base Galactic Crusader parts into higher detailed versions that will allow those of you with 8k and 12k printers to showcase your models with. In addition, the figures are easily to print at 200% (maybe even 400%?) for use with other games systems and scales.

The blender source is included containing my hobo-rigged figures and pose library. I wasn't feeling all too well and took some liberties/shortcuts than I would for a more generic release but should get you most of the way even when I used basic object parenting for a few parts. Sorry =/

Figures have been run through 3DBuilder to merge and decimate the meshes to reasonable levels though you can export your own from the Blend. I've also uploaded a zip of just the unmerged undecimated figures for your further use if so desired. Not that plinths, risers, and banner icons are NOT merged so you can rework or replace stuff as works for you.

Big shouts out to Moonjam for the base content to build on. Icons from Lord Chronos. Heads based on work from M3rcurymordbid.

If you like what I did and want to leave a tip it would be appreciated.

Update: I changed them to be 2mm high, the bottom is now 0,4mm high and the outer walls still 0,8.
They're now perfect to print with a 0,4mm nozzle and 0,2mm layer height.
I added all the earlier 1,5mm versions to a zip file, they still work perfectly fine.

Annoyed by having to fill the little gaps on hole bases for infantry models or by adding to much mass on top when adding more creative base designs?
Look no further! These bases have huge holes instead of small ones, so you can just fill the entire top of the base with Green Stuff/Milliput/Tamiya-Putty or whatever you like!

They're probably best printed with FDM but they should also work with SLA printers, I only tested them with FDM so far.

!MAKE SURE TO LET THEM COOL OFF INSTEAD OF PULLING THEM OFF THE BUILDPLATE WHILE THEY'RE STILL WARM OR THEY WILL END UP BEING BENT!

I used pretty old dried up Green Stuff for the example picture, so please excuse that it looks terrible.

If you want any other size just post a coment and I'll make it for you.

Here's my set of modular building elements that allows you to build gothic-like structures for your wargaming terrain. I designed it for FDM printers.

The initial idea was to be able to create simple gothic-like walls in both undamaged and damaged form, so this is the reason why there are no floor tiles just yet.

There are no fancy connecting mechanism - use the glue, Luke! I prefer to use quick-drying basing glue.

**1.0v - Initial Release**

- Includes 27 wall and column modules.

**Updates**

- 18-07-2023: after some more printing, I can confirm that resizing the modules down to 80% still works great. I can also confirm that the modules print easily on a resin printer - with no supports, placed directly on the build plate. To save resin, you can hollow the columns (don't forget to add the drainage holes).

When building Gore Krusha Mega Walkers, greenskin Meks sometimes opt to build massive klanky klaws as melee weapons instead of the often-seen giant saws.


FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

This highly detailed Klaw Arm is compatible to my Gore Krusha's Mega Walker
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/gore-krusha-mega-walker

I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.050 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.
Please see the pics of my print, those are all in FDM (0,05mm layer height)!

I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I recommend it to use them on some parts - decide for yourself & make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 (layer height) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer height 0.05 to 0.075(!) )


----------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: --------------------
----------------------------------------------------------------------

---------- MOVABLE PARTS ----------
- Most pivot points are actually functional, pose the arm as you want!
- I have included a functional hydraulics option for the klaw, so it can move once assembled.
 -> You need a well calibrated printer to get this hydraulics working. Print all *FlexHydraulics*.stl with wallcount = e.g. 99 to get a massive print without infill.
 -> For the FlexHydraulics pins you need to cut of ca. 10mm of regular 1,75mm filament. (I did not test this in resin, but I guess you could print them)
 -> As an option to the FlexHydraulics there are two fixed versions. Have a look in the parts.
- Print all PINS with wallcount = e.g. 99 to get a massive print without infill.

---------- CABLES and WIRES ----------

KlawArm_03 Bits come with an option to glue in some wires (or filament).
If you use some 0,75mm² or 0,5mm² electrical wires the arm could still be movable :)

---------- Arm on the LEFT or RIGHT? ----------
You can print all parts normally except the shoulder pauldrons. (because of the flat printing side)
-> You have to mirror both pauldrons if you want the arm on the left side of your model (from your point of view)

---------- ASSEMBLY ----------

If you need instructions - just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where they need to go.

---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for some coins for caffeine I need doin' stuff like that :-)

Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of 80h+ of free time!
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

I'm not a fan of the traditional plastic flight stands for flying miniatures. They tend to be brittle and weak in my experience.

This was designed in TinkerCAD Codeblocks so that is can be easily adjusted to fit the size you want.

https://www.tinkercad.com/codeblocks/a8A3BhQCXXA

The idea to glue the 3D printed dome base onto a washer for weight, and glue a nail into the hole in the dome.

I am using commonly available fender washer sizes and 4G nails. There is a magnet in to bottom of the space ship.


The space ship is by Tezca.

Tiny tanks! The perfect thing to give a sense of scale to your tiny titans, tiny aircraft, or tiny anything! Add them as base decoration, add them as terrain decoration, create tiny war dioramas, do whatever you want with them! Anything is made better with the addition of tiny tanks.

Tiny tanks are intended for resin printers.

Provides a version of Woddish's excellent Tiny Tank Classic Mbt (now gone), KMFP proto-rhino concept, and a Scorpios launcher of unknown source, and a radar from Chris John, that have been sliced into major parts that are enabled to be quickly swapped and edited for customization by changing visibility of components between different options for hatches, side doors, symbols/icons, and crew. The eventual end game would be the ability to build any Deimos based Monoceros chassis vehicle with this tool.

This is intended for designers and modelers to product their own faction customized vehicles from in a standardized and high quality form.

If you like what I did and want to leave a tip it would be appreciated.
https://paypal.me/jimmyzimms

Edit 20220526: Found some flipped normals I missed and a couple of positioning errors so corrected. Since 3D Builder gets annoyed about nonmanifold object and does the wrong thing occasionally I've updated all the parts, even if it shouldn't matter.

Edit 20230112: Added a slicer for the side doors to the blender file that can be used by designers to make form fitting symbols from that can be set into the hatches.

Edit 20230426: Added support for KMFP's nifty 3rd edition style Whirlwind Launcher

Edit 20230519: With permission, incorporated thewraeththu's better Scorpius into the builder.

Edit 20230908: Updated the Scorpius launcher to have an upper deck based on the Deimos predator. This better matches to the updated plastic kit from GW.

Edit 20240117: Minor cleanup

Edit 20240518: For those that like rivets and bolts, two sets (based on the geometry of each glacis option) have been added to adorn your tanks with tons of extra! Thanks TC63 for the contributions!

Edit 20241027: Added in crew from the Rapax From Deimos builder here.

6mm skimmer skiffs for your tiny evil space elves to fly amock and be absolute jerks to everybody.

This set includes

3 hull variants, each with transport and gunship versions.
4 sail variants, with hole for 2x1mm round magnet or a simple peg
6 different drivers to steer the skiff towards your targets
6 bow gunners each with a shadow laser and disintegration beam option.
6 side gunners for extra mayhem, each with 2 weapon options.
3 styles of bases, plain, net and blade, each in 3 poses.

The sails can be printed with a peg and glued in place, but I recommend using 2x1 round magnets, this makes them much less likely to break off, and you can pose and swap them if you feel like it.

Supported files are currently NOT included. The bases should print without supports but the rest will need to be supported before printing.

The detail on these should look good to about 15mm if scaled up, any larger (like 28mm) and they will start to look awfully bobblehead and disproportion.

Hopefully more to come soon!

The All-Purpose Carrier lives up to its name as a rugged and dependable platform that has been adapted to almost every role on & off the battlefield.

This all-in-one package of M'khand-pattern All-Purpose Carrier parts allows you to build your ideal APC-based vehicle to your exact needs. Contains all previously released APC-chassis related files***, both free and paid, adapted to 1:300 scale for mass-scale wargames.

Turrets and middles have 2.5x1.25mm holes for magnets. Compatible with all epic scale M'khand-pattern APC & Lemoine Russel turrets.

To use meshmixer builder, open with meshmixer (a free program from autodesk) and ctrl-click in the object browser the items you wish to have as one piece. Then go to File and Export. Your merged piece is ready for repair and slicing.

Alternatively, individual part stls can be assembled in 3Dbuilder or another program of your choice where they should snap together.

***Non-IFV turrets, Christie suspension sides and artillery cannons for unarmoured hulls not included***

Tiny tanks! The perfect thing to give a sense of scale to your tiny titans, tiny aircraft, or tiny anything! Add them as base decoration, add them as terrain decoration, create tiny war dioramas, do whatever you want with them! Anything is made better with the addition of tiny tanks.

We've long since jumped the shark when it comes to tiny biggest tank designs. But just in case you're one of those tiny generals who is sure that more gunz is even better here's the overcompensation tank.

Tiny tanks are intended for resin printers.

You should print 1 chassis, 4 point defense turrets, and 2 main turrets (one mirrored) for each tank you want.

A heavily reworked version of the awesome TINY BIGGEST TANK MBT by Woddish with custom glacis and turrets crafted to visually resemble the design cues of the Tiny Bigger Tank MBT to bridge the two designs. The main turret is fully interchangeable with that tank (for additional modeling joy). The smaller turrets will fully work with my TINY BIGGEST TANK REDUX as well. This was inspired by the brilliant 40k kitbash as well as the classic 2nd Edition epic figure.

Blender source included!

Update 20221222: TheZomby has graciously provided not one but two new alternate main turrets for our use! Big ups!

Update 2023.04.03: Added an additional hatch on the upper deck of the chassis. The area looked a little empty of details in real life.

Gore Krushas are build by the biggest and craziest meks at the peak of a greenskin WAAAAAGH! as a symbol of their gods - Towering over the battlefield this 'eavy armored walker krushes smaller enemies by simply stomping them to bloody goo (with insane laughter from the Gore Kursha Kaptin').
Meanwhile larger targets can be engaged with it's mega chain choppa, ripping through armor easily.
Although not very accurate, the Gore Krushas ranged weapons have 'nuff shootin' to hit and kill all targets. The sound of high kaliber gattlas at full auto bursts is horrifying or at least intimidating for the most enemies (....or motivating in case of greenskin ears)


FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

To print the Gore Krusha Mega Walker, you need time or a large resin printer ;-)
I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.
Please see the pics, those are all printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!

I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I recommend it to use them on some parts - decide for yourself & make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 (layer hight) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 to 0.075(!) )
(The Mega Choppa should be printed with tree support, I included a version with the teef supported, this is also tested)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: --------------------
----------------------------------------------------------------------

---------- SPIKES ----------

Print them "laying", not standing, or else they will easily snap of if you ram another model ;-)

---------- Exhausts ----------

"GoreKrusha_Exhausts02_Bars_1.75mmFilament.stl" can be combined with "GoreKrusha_Exhausts02.stl" for Resin printers.
In FDM just use some 1.75mm filament & make sure you don't snap of the middle post - trust me :D

---------- LEGS ----------

The legs can be posed standing or walking, but I recommend standing for both to find a good balance for the model.

---------- ARMS ----------

- !!! All joints MUST be printed laying flat !!! This is important, else they will likely snap of due to the weight of the arms.
- The arms should fit thight, but they are not perfect, better glue them after posing
- The ammo belt is a "flexi" print-in-place, once finished, you can gently move the joints to breake it free. With this, the dakka arm can be posed freely as you want.

---------- DA RIGGAZ (Crew) ----------

- Da Riggaz are posed and remixed from https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3985624 by poikilos
- To print Da Riggaz you need tree supports, I flipped them back 15° or 30° (depending on the model) and lifted them +1,5mm on the Z-axies, so the supports will pe printed first. Layer hight 0.05mm, enable support roof with ~0.75mm.

---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------

- I printed the bottom plate with 25% infill, since it has to carry the weight of the model (about 1,2kg!)
- Many parts have a "flat surface" -> face those to the build plate.
- Detaild sides / most visible sides should be faced towards the cooling fan.

---------- ASSEMBLY ----------

If you need instructions - just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where they go.

An improved pattern of the M'khand Pattern Lemoine Russel Battle Tank, with improved suspension and internal layout offering more crew comfort and higher accuracy when firing on the move. Comes with all turret coxial and sponson weapon options offered at larger scales for maximum customisation.

Completed bodies, turrets and middles have 2.5x1.25mm holes for magnets. Compatible with all epic scale M'khand-pattern Lemoine Russel parts and variants. Comes with a variety of decals and effects.

The zip includes all my parts and meshmixer files. With Meshmixer (free program from Autodesk), simply Shift+Click the pieces you want to use and select export under the FILE dropdown menu. Alternatively, parts can be assembled via 3dBuilder, Blender or another software of your choice. Exported pieces are then ready for repair in netfab/3dbuilder/prusaslicer and slicing.

For best results when printing destroyed turrets, include a closed hatch with the turret, weapon and smoke to prevent a small pocket of unprinted resin.

__For printing for LIMP/AT18, increase scale to 125% when slicing__

2023-12-03: Added new options for side weapons and a builder with all my other lemoine russel variants in it.

2023-12-07: Added adapters to fit the turrets to plastic LIMP hulls. Combine with other wanted parts before scaling up 125%

2023-12-07: Split hull weapon mounts from the hulls. Added new hull weapon options. Removed the old redundant builder file.

2024-01-14: Added coronal-designations of the three patterns of turret as well as both a turret-mounted heat ray and heavy flamethrower.

2024-08-24: Added internal side sponsons.

The Excess God: Demon Chariots 5.0 bundle delivers a brutal and decadent vision of war at 10mm scale, featuring three distinct demon chariot models forged to embody speed, excess, and merciless destruction on the battlefield. Each chariot is designed with aggressive silhouettes, dynamic motion, and exaggerated details that remain crisp and readable even at small scale, making them ideal centerpieces for dark fantasy or infernal-themed armies.

Every model in this bundle is carefully optimized for high-quality resin printing. All miniatures come manually pre-supported using Lychee Slicer, with supports placed by hand to ensure reliable prints, minimal cleanup, and maximum preservation of fine details. The geometry is engineered to reduce unnecessary islands while maintaining structural strength, allowing for efficient and consistent printing across multiple copies.

These miniatures are created for miniature-agnostic tabletop games, giving players full freedom to use them across a wide range of custom systems and settings. They are not intended to replace, replicate, or act as proxies for any commercially licensed miniature ranges. For non-agnostic games, the use of original, officially licensed components is always recommended. Tordominis does not condone or support piracy in any form.

All distribution rights for these models are reserved exclusively by Tordominis. Official releases are available only through the Tordominis store on MyMiniFactory and through authorized physical miniature sellers. Any unauthorized sharing or distribution of these files, including via third-party websites, file-sharing platforms, or messaging services, is strictly prohibited.

This bundle is built for players and collectors seeking uncompromising detail, dark grandeur, and battlefield presence at epic scale.

I've never been keen on the current model for this. The older resin version was better, but better still was the late 90s version by Tim Adcock. I've tried to recreate that version but using modern Space Elf designs.

The bulk of the model is Lord Cronos's beam hover tank from here:
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/tiny-space-elves-beam-hover-tank
With the hover tank turret from here:
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/tiny-space-elves-hover-tank
The fins at the back of the hull are based on the ones from this model:
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/sprue-eldar-hornet
The dispensers are taken from here:
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/space-elf-support-quasi-classic-platform-weapons

The model is the same scale as Lord Chronos's model on which it is based. For a more traditional 6mm scale, print it scaled to 80%.

The holes in the dispenser will probably need drilling out slightly to fit onto the mounting on the turret. The models all ought to fit but in practice I found that they don't. Alternatively try merging the web spinners with the turret and printing it as one piece.

Here and there the model is quite fragile, so take care when removing supports, assembling the parts or just handling the model.

Quite a bit larger than an Imperial Baneblade, a Kill Grinda Mega Fortress is truly a fearsome idol of the brutish Ork gods:
On massive, krushin' trakks, armed with weapons capable of destroying entire hab blocks with one shot, they rumble onwards, where da fORKtress Kaptains points them to.
Only the most powerful Warbosses have 'nuff teef to pay the bestest meks to build these mega-super-heavy assault vehicles.

An IMPORTANT note for the scale :D
- Quote of an imperial agent during a massive Ork encounter on Fungusius Primus:
"Big Mek Gutgrinda once build this thing at a scale of a Baneblade (~79%).... he was KRUSHED and GRINDED brutally to deff by WAAAGHBOSS Gobba Gitkrusha's 'GORKAfORKress' (100% scale)" ;-)



----------------------------------------------------------------------
------- FOR BEST PRINT QUALITY , PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW: --------
----------------------------------------------------------------------

I REALLY recommend a layer hight of 0.075 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.
Please see the pics, those are all printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!

All parts are printed without tree supports, some parts don't need supports, but please decide for your self. :)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
---------------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: ------------------
----------------------------------------------------------------------

---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------

Many parts have a "flat surface" -> face those to the build plate. Keep in mind, the z-axies does the detailed job!
Detailed sides / most visible sides should be faced towards the cooling fan.

The supa gattla can fit two 5x3mm magnet to be rotatable. The "KillGindaMegaFortress_SupaGattla_Pin.stl" does a similar job, but not as good, I guess... although I never tested the magnets.

The main gun can be assembled in 3 ways:
- Mega Zzappa
- Nukular Shell (with or without spacer, as you like)
- None of both

I printed the supa gattla ammo without a raft, but if you have problems with adhesion, use a raft.
-> If you have concerns about the sharp corners of the ammo belt in FMD, you have the right feeling, but "in the end it doesn't matter", you will not see this issue after assembly.
-> enable "print thin walls" in cura or equivalent in your slicer.

Arrange the lobbas ("KillGrindaMegaFortress_Lobbas02 - 07 & _LazerMarker) as you like, view all files in e.g. 3D Builder or Meshmixer to see how I designed them. The "Lazer sight"-bit is optional, you can replace it with an additional lobba as you like.

---------- Assembly ----------

All parts have a arritation point, so just "move" them until they snap or feel right.
- If you need instructions: just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where all parts belong to.


---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-)

Not the best weapon for Smaller Knights, but I am a completionist. This is the last one on my list.

The C-Beamer is a relic weapon usually overlooked because it does more damage the farther away the target is, and less up close, which is a disadvantage on the close-range, terrain-choked tabletops of the current edition.

But, it's free. ;)

Supported versions have a lot of tiny sub-supports that you will want to flick out after curing, especially on barrel 3. It seemed the only way to save that spiraling effect.

You might not be able to access or paint the interior cages of barrels 2 or 3. If that is unacceptable, I recommend barrel 1. It's cleaner and sleeker.

Everything is included from the shoulder socket down.

Ball and socket upper arms are included, in case you want to keep a fixed, glued pose.

I recommend the flat-elbowed upper arms, and magnetizing with an 8mm x 2mm or 8mm x 3mm neodymium magnet glued to the fused upper arm, and steel magnets glued to the elbow "socket" of the weapon.

I usually glue a steel BB in the socket, then cap it with a pair of glued-on steel washers. See pics for reference.

You'll lose some poseability, but gain modularity.

Also, check out my other mech and knight parts, most of which are free.
https://cults3d.com/en/users/johnbearross/creations

Enjoy!

Best,
JBR

Want to fire some flesh eatin' short range artillery ammunishun that's not a bug?? Rukka Buggys are your vehicle of choice! Slap it! Expolode it!
"How much bity or 'splodin' flesh balls you want to shoot??" - "Yes."


FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

To print the Rukka Buggy, you need time or a resin printer ;-)
I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075mm or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.
Please see the pics, those are all printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!

I highly recommend it to use tree supports (at least on the crew) - make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 (layer hight) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 (crew) or 0.075mm (buggy))

---------- Over all printing recommendation (FDM) ----------

- Many parts have a flat surface -> face those to the build plate. Print slow (25mm/s)
- Detaild sides / most visible sides should be faced towards the cooling fan.
- Crew should be printed with tree supports, rotated 45° back (so the face is up). Support Z-distance should be a multiple of 2 to 3 of the layer hight (0.05 - 0.075mm). PRINT SLOW - Outer wall max 25mm/s. You want dem details gooood!

The most difficult parts (actually not the Gobbo Crew...):
- "RuckaBuggy_Rear_02.stl": you need to be super carefull to remove tree supports (they are needed). My test print broke on the bars while removing them. I was able to glue it back on (tip: smooth cracks with a lighter)
- "RuckaBuggy_Front_04.stl": failed 4 times while removing tree supports, combined with other parts. I needed to print this part as a single part with normal supports.

---------- Assembly ----------

If you need instructions - just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where they go.
Some parts are press fits (e.g. the wheels) you don't need to glue them, unless you print in resin (not tested).
I recommend to "dry fit" the parts with blu tack or a similar reusable putty.


---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for => "Tossin' a coin to your Tersus...." :D

Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of many hours of free time!
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-) :-) :-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

Loads of containers and container handling goodness! Stationary container cranes, walking container cranes, quad container haulers, container skates, container land trains, and more! A variety of container stacks! A confusing plethora of files! These containers and handling equipment make a great container yard terrain setup, or just lots of small vehicles and scatter terrain to give your battlefields some life.

Models include:
The big stationary container crane is presented in several models, with the container 'rack' in different positions. A seperate part is included for a container hanging from cables.

Quad mech 'walking' container cranes in several models. They can also use the hanging container part if you print the version with no rack. (Its another quad industrial mech!)

The container Train is a multi-part model of a tractor and one or more trailers to make up a 'train' that is meant to service the stationary cranes. Empty trailers are included along with those loaded with one or two containers.

Container Stackers are trucks with piston lifts that allow them to drive over single containers, or lift high enough to double-stack. Handy for moving containers but can't stack as high as the big walking cranes.

Container skates are a variation of the mech skates (see the mech repair posting!) either loaded or unloaded; they're an alternative to the trains for moving containers and look best when being loaded/unloaded by the walking cranes.

Container stacks in different configurations and heights, along with a few single containers.

A Buildermech with a container flatbed is also included (See my Buildermech posting for lots of other options - the crane version would also be handy in a container yard. Also, see my modular ships to have something the big cranes can offload!

Modeled in 6mm scale.

Our biggest project is alive!


The challenge was to create a AT scale and a 40K scale hyperdetailed Imperator titan remix.


- The model is a remix from only public or free STLs so it can be shared freely


- The titan is inspired in the Titandeath novel cover, with flat upper platform and gothic style similar to the old classic Epic design.


- Size: 25 cms. for AT, for 40K, following FW scale, it should have a hight of 95-105 cms. so you should upscale the models at 400% or use the 40K scale version. You can upscale it up to 2mts to keep with the lore.


- The base used model is the old epic imperator model, a fantastic and totally accurate model from creator dantigibus you can find (yet) free on cults Here: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/titan-imperator


- The other base model is the imperator titan, modern-style, from creator zammerak you can find also free here in Cults: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/titanic-church-delivery-system


- The first part finished was the head, 40K scale with detailed interiors you can download here in Cults in my collection. This release features a AT scale head with no interiors.


- Inside the .zip file you can find a construction guide.





- If you want to know the history of this project, step by step, go to my web page: http://inquisitorweb.mygamesonline.org in the crazy mixer section.





- I'm trying to cut the 40K scale parts to fit Saturn printers. By now, the larger part fits in Saturn 2 printer. Some bigger ones could not fit in the old Saturn.





- Enjoy! and remember donations are always welcome! help us further development of this model.





WARNING! This is a very challenging model, only suitable for very experienced printers and modellers.





Users with a 8K printer may choose to use the 40K version for AT downscaling every part to -400%.





Changelog:





17-4-22: Reinforced the base of the platform down spires, they were too thin for printing in a 2K printer.


18-4-22: Rebuild the upper gun towers. Some people had issues printing them, so I,ve splitted each tower in 2 parts (3 for the back towers) and extra-repair both of them.


Now the problems seems to be solved.


24-4-22: Added 2 optional buildings, a tower bridge in front of the main basillica, and a curved bridge tower for the sides.


27-4-22: last updates, 2 small optional towers for the central place in the platform (place at your choice), replacement fences for the tiny torso fences (sides and back) and church circular fences that don't print well in 2K printers and also replacements for the tiny tower windows.


And as a reward only for my kindly donators, an optional landing pad for the back of the platform with a Arvus lighter included! Ask me for the parts.


27-8-22 Added a set of alternative arms for the main weapons, created by Andrew Killoch


30-10-22 Added a file with the ongoing 40K scale parts, WIP. just now only leg armour, feet and part of the bastion.


6-11-22 Added an alternative 2 parts splitted AT scale torso for smaller printers and uploaded the last leg parts in 40K scale. Now, the legs are complete in 40K scale. and made to the max detail limits my (rather old) computer allows me.


11-11-22 Plasma anihilator complete in 40K scale, find it in the 40K scale file.


20-11-22 Hellstorm cannon complete in 40K scale,find it in the 40K scale file.


3-12-22 Added the head for 40K scale, a revision from my Imperator head model in Cults, size reduced to fit the Imperator body to AT X 4, more detailed and with a simplified top with better fit with the lower middle parts. The head comes without crew.


Also in the main weapons folders you can find both arms (take care, they are different, not mirrors).


4-12-22 Added a 40K scale head variation with crew integrated (2 moderatii and 1 princeps) in the donators rewards folder.


14-12-22 Added a 40K scale Chaos head variant in the donators folder with demonic crew inside.


16-12-22 The 40K torso parts are complete! splitted to fit in a Saturn S or Saturn 2 printer. Added too an alternative part with a secret toaster repair dock in the donators folder. Enjoy!


18-12-22 Added the left feet missing parts (the feet part 4 isn't a mirror from the right one)


5-2-23 Plattform base in 40K scale released! with optional tower splitted parts. As usual parts are splitted to fit larger printers as Saturn 2.


5-3-23 Main cathedral, the first platform building finished!


20-3-23 Started painting the AT scale printed prototype


15-4-23 The Quake cannon Bastion, second platform bulding, finished


21-4-23 Next set of platform buildings ready in 40K scale: Volcano cannon tower and small side church (X2).


2-5-23 Finished the Optional rounded bridge in 40K scale with his rail AA gun and the optional small bridge too.


8-5-23 Last platform buldings finished: front and rear towers and side small tower. Also added in the donators rewards folder a new, remixed Arvus lighter and the optional rear landing platform in 40K scale.


9-5-23 Model finished!!!! yuhuuu!!! last 40K scale parts: the towers under the platform and the hips version 2 (without the emblematic dick cannon)


10-5-23 Added an optional right torso part 6 variant with mechanicum WC and amno rooms in the donators reward forlder.


17-5-23 Added an optional left torso part 4 variant with mechanicum vending machine in the donators reward forlder and repair some minor errors in front and rear towers lower parts (front tower part 1 and rear tower part 3)


19-5-23 Repaired some minor errors in left leg bastion part 3 and added some more details.


22-5-23 Add an alternative AA gun for the platform, more detailed, remixed from redzabo free model on Cults

A free upgrade kit for your smaller knight models, released along with the Project Abby conversion kit found here...

https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/project-abby-conversion-kit-for-naughty-knights

Included in this kit are...

-FOUR nasty blades, including three chain weapons and a cleaner-looking power weapon.

-FIVE claws, including a pincer with dual saws.

-Three triple-missile launchers in vertical, horizontal, and triangular configurations. Two poses are offered: straight ahead, and tilted back for launch.

-UPDATE: The missile launchers were a little big for my taste, so I have included 12 new files (supported and clean) for launchers reduced about 15%. Either can be used. Also, if you're using the mounting peg, some sanding/filing may be necessary, especially after paint.

-Three main weapon bodies, with three degrees of tilt.

-Two forearm weapons extensions.

-Five Suturus Pattern upper arms at various fixed angles. The upper arms twist-lock to fit with factory kits.

Note: This upgrade kit requires a small amount of hobby time and effort.
I recommend you magnetize the upper arms at the elbow flat with a 8mm-wide diameter x 3mm- or 2mm-thick magnet.
I would then glue steel washers to the top of the main weapon body.

Thanks!

Best, JBR

Please use these files and their resulting prints for private use only, unless you have secured a production license. Gracias.

Supported and Clean versions of all files are in the zipped folders.

Originally designed as an upgrade to a Factory kit, Project Abby has now been sculpted to be its own full frame, armor, weaponry, and escort drones.
Past purchasers of the Project Abby (check the URL) upgrade kit are now rewarded for their early support with a free upgrade.
Thank you very much!

----------------------------

With the mysterious Dark Powers making their once-hidden presence more known, new, sinister mech designs have begun to appear on the battlefields of the Junctionworld inter-reality gate networks.

Notable among these new nightmares is a tailed, tentacled monstrosity labeled by intel operatives at the Mercenary Guild as Project Abby.

These warped, spiked, and twisted armors are malevolent in form and purpose. They have a heat cannon on one arm as their primary ranged weapon, while the melee component of their arsenal is composed of an energized whip weapon system. Crackling with plasma, this cluster of mechanical tentacles can be used to impale, crush, or slice through enemy targets. The Abby features a tail-like appendage that performs the same function, protecting the armored walker from the rear.

Project Abby mechs also seem to be nesting grounds for ScytheBots, verminous robot drones that seem to claim the dreaded hulks as mobile nests. These hive-like bots provide a symbiotic layer of protection for the mech, cutting down infantry that venture too close.

Some time ago I was felt very inspired by the 40K scale imperator titan from Zammerak you can find here in Cults, so I started remixing my own head variant, more close to the titan in the Titandeath cover, a design closer to the original Epic imperator model and featuring a full detailed interior cockpit. I used for the remix the head from the zammerak´s titan and a low poly faceplate model here in cults, apart from hundreds of bits from Cults and Thingiverse for the interior detailing.
The size is calibrated to lore 40K scale titan, of about 95-110 cms. It´s compatible with my Imperator model and Grant´s model but it will need to be rescalated about -25%
In the plans if fits OK but when I´ve printed it needed a lot of sanding in the cap part :-( Version 2 features a simplified cap with better fit.
The interior features complete cockpit with monitors, controls, a holographic display and a hiden room bellow with as little chapel and 2 servitors. Hope you like it :-) Complete crew (2 moderatii and 1 princeps) in the donators rewars folder.

This model is remixed from this models:

- For the base I used zammerak´s titan head, you can fin the complete titan in Cults free Here: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/titanic-church-delivery-system
- For the faceplate I choose this model from Fantabuloustexan, Here free in Cults3D: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/various/walkin-church-titan-head
- And hundreds of bits from Thingiverse and Cults3D

25-11-22 Added 3 neck versions for using in different imperator bodies sizes and a instructionsTXT
4-12-22 Added new head version 2! size adapted to my Imperator body (AT scale X 4), more detailed and with a simplified cap with better fit.

I am releasing this for free, please feel free to donate or buy your filament using the affiliate link (see the readme) to support this massive project.

The Gorkabot is a massive armored mech, built as an effigy of a greenskin god! Armed to da teef da Gorkabot krushes all kind of ememys with it's klaw while shredding infantry with hails of bullets from the DAKKA-Storm gun.


In the Gorkabots belly is space for a few greenskins to pop out, if the time is good for some krumpin'!








FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:





To print the Gorkabot, you need time or a resin printer ;-)


I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.


Please see the pics, those are all printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!





I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I highly recommend it to use them - make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 (layer hight) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 to 0.075(!) )








----------------------------------------------------------------------


-------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: ----------


----------------------------------------------------------------------








---------- COMPATIBILITY ----------





Arms and legs should be compatible to my Mega Bots (not testet)





---------- MAIN BODY ----------





"GorkaBot_Belly.stl" prints without tree support! Just use regular supports.


"GorkaBot_Torso.stl" prints without tree support! Just use regular supports. flip the model slightly to the back (see Cura screenshot)


The doors should be printed without supports with a brim (see Cura screenshot)





---------- LEGS ----------





The legs are unique, there is an individual model for the right / left leg. Those are mirrorable / interchangeable if you want.





---------- ARMS----------





The arms should fit 10x4mm magnets (not tested) but also have a ball joint for more posability...





The "GorkaBot_Klaw_Arm_02.stl" should be printed 45° "floating 1,5mm in the air" see my Cura screenshot - this will give you the best quality result!





---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------





Many parts have a "flat surface" -> face those to the build plate.


Detaild sides / most visible sides should be faced towards the cooling fan.





---------- Assembly ----------





if you need instructions - just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where they go








---------- FOLLOWING: ----------





Shame less beggin' for some coins for coffein I need doin' stuff like that :-D ;-)





Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of 100h+ of free time!


If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-) :-) :-)





Kind regards,


Tersus

**Go to the "Thing Files" tab to individually download the files - Thingiverse is giving an odd 404 error when trying to use the "Download all files" buttons**

The perfect restaurant for watching S7 broadcasts or kicking back with the local mercs for a beer. This building is designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support placing units on top in all hexes for playability. The top of version B has additional supports for two edge hexes for extra stability. It is 1 level tall in most areas, except for the front two hexes where it is 1.5 levels tall, if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

There are eight files. For each of version A and B, one has the building on hexes, another is hexless so that you can print the one that fits your playstyle, and there are two more versions that have the text removed from the front of the building. Using the NoText versions, you can paint custom names on the front, print off logos to attach, or leave it blank.

As always, tipping is appreciated at: paypal.me/rainingfire416

Notable features:
-An in-universe themed restaurant name.
-Fantastic custom logo and details to give it a proper BBQ joint look.
-Detailed design including doors, windows, and a detailed roof with greebles.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.

This is a shoulder/carapace mounted Turbolaser Destructor (twin turbolaser) for use with Stroganoff's Battleduke Warstrider model.

It's a mashup of this Apocalypse Rocket Launcher by totenpf:
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4814519
...the turbolaser barrels from this Wardog:
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/lucius-wardog-titan
...and part of the Laser Blaster model that comes with the Battleduke
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/epic-scale-mars-warlord-titan

I took all the bits, chopped them around, scaled them to fit and mashed them together.

It should fit exactly onto the Battleduke model if you print them both at the same scale. If you want to use it with an AT-scale model you'll need to scale it up a bit; probably about 125% but I don't know exactly as I haven't tried it and I don't currently have any AT models to measure.

The model is slightly asymmetrical. I think it works better on the right shoulder; mirror it for the left.

This is an enormous two-bladed close combat saw weapon for huge battle robots. It comes in four pieces - the actual saw part, an elbow joint, an upper arm piece, and the shoulder joint. You can simply superglue the parts together to achieve the handedness and posing you wish. The shoulder joint has a built-in half-socket for a 5mm disc magnet, and the saw is essentially symmetrical so it'll look just as good as a left or right arm (though you may want to keep which side you'll want to use it for in mind while you're planning your supports). The arm can be built as either a left or right arm.

As this is based on a handful of different (free) sources, I'm offering it for free:

The saw blade itself is from the Armor Bearer Saw by Arajar: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3989916

And the actual arm is 40K Big Reaper Titan AT Style Chainfist by The_Titan_Manufactorium: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/40k-big-reaper-titan-at-style-chainfist

This is a generic upper arm piece compatible with my RV-A series of guns. It's based on a model I found floating around on the internet - unfortunately I can't find the creator, but kudos to whoever made it - with a few modifications, so here it is for free for convenience's sake.

There are five variants, choose whichever fits your purposes:

RV Arm is the original model as-is.
RV Arm Elbow Magnet has a magnet well for a 5x1mm disc magnet cut into the lower end of the arm.
RV Arm Shoulder Magnet cuts the ball joint for the shoulder in half and adds a half-socket for a 5mm disc magnet to the top surface.
RV Arm Double Magnet has both the elbow magnet well and the shoulder half-socket.
Finally, the RV Arm Plug has a shoulder half-socket and a slightly-less-than-5mm diameter plug built into the elbow surface that'll fit into the magnet well of my RV-A series of guns.

The Skrappin' Mega Bot is a stompin' armored Mech capable of moving objects without any efforts using it's powerfull trakktor kannon! Dead 'ard

killy saws tear apart every enemy getting to close. Once the Skrappin' Mega Bot krushed some enemy vehicles, turing those into piles of skrapp, it 

can do some quick n' dirty fixin' jobs on allied vehicles or mechs.


FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

Beneath my Krumpin' Mega Bot this is one of my most detailed models until now!

To print this monster, you need time or a resin printer ;-)
I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended, while designing this model - please see the pics, those

are printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!

I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I highly recommend it to use them - make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2

(layer hight) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 to 0.075(!) )

For a few bitz I added a resin version with "_Resin" in the file name - unlike the FDM versions those don't have a flat bottom. (I have not test printed 

these files, but they should be good to go!)

The Trakktor Kannon can be a variant of an actuall (rattling) Kannon, as it lifts up 'eavy objects and throw them with a high velocity to enemy gitz - 

less explosiv, more smashin' - same damage! ;-)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
---------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: ----------
----------------------------------------------------------------------


---------- COMPATIBILITY ----------

Most parts are compatible to my Krumpin' Mega Bot, so you can build your variant as you like :)
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/krumpin-mega-bot

---------- MAIN BODY ----------

You CAN use two 10x4mm Neodym magnets for the junction "hip <> main hull" to get a rotatable/removable body!
As an alternative to the magnets print the file "ScrappinMegaBot_Hip02.stl"

---------- LEGS ----------

The legs are unique, there is a individual model for the right / left leg. Those are mirrorable / interchangeable if you want.

---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------

Many parts have a "flat surface" - face those to the build plate.

---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for some coins for coffein I need doin' stuff like that :-D ;-)

Please consider a tip ....this HIGH detailed model was a work of 80h+ of free time!
This model is not a simple remix, all parts of my Krumpin' Mega Bot have been reviewed and altered with new details! :-)
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-) :-):-)

Designed up this dealer button to use in home games or have just as something laying around for any poker fan. It was inspired by a dealer button in Pokerstars VR.

Printing:

Ring - Infil to add weight, supports needed for spade inset. Letter embossing doesn't need it.
Spade - Infil to add weight, no supports

A free model as a way of giving back to the hobby.

Do you like dealing out mortal wounds?

I've got a nice heat cannon for all your chooming needs.

Intended for Smaller Knights. Magnetization is suggested, using 8mm x 2mm magnets across the flats, 4mm magnets in the elbow pockets, or steel washers.

Included are...
Three cannons with different mounting angles at the elbow.
Five Upper Arms compatible with factory models.

Sorry, Waldo, my reference model, is not part of the package. He's made of a mixture of different models, and is used for size reference only for a generic 28mm fig.

Enjoy!

Best,
John Bear Ross/JBR

I want to thank you folks for helping me reach 500 followers after only a month of paid sales.

As a token of appreciation, here's the RFBC-500 Avtomat Pushka (sorry, my computer-translated Russian is terrible), an Automatic Rifle Cannon (RFBC proxy).

It's available in both Right (A) and Left (B) versions, with the main weapon body having a choice of stick or drum magazine.

Also, one of my heavy stubby gatlings is incorporated into the design. That asymmetric part of the design is a nice feature, in my opinion.

A pair of weapon arms, long and short, are supplied, as well as upper arms at a variety of angles for magnetization.

I glue the ball and sockets together, then glue 12mm x 2mm magnets to the bottom of the upper arm.

An 8mm x 2mm magnet will fit in the face of the main weapon body. I usually glue in washers in the barrel section. 4mm inner diameter/9mm outer diameter washers usually do it, or #6 washers. Or just glue them together and print more.

You can use opposing magnets in the weapon arms (remember opposite poles) to the new upper arms. I recommend 12mm x 3mm magnets.

Enjoy, and thanks again! More good stuff to come.

Best,
JBR

P.S. Check out my other Knight parts, most of which are free.
https://cults3d.com/en/users/johnbearross/creations

P.P.S. I started a Discord server for feedback and for folks to follow progress of my sculpts.
https://discord.gg/NJtm78rF63

2
3
4
5
6

It's a big quad industrial mech! The Drillermech is a BIG mech (for 6mm anyway), intended to operate as an all terrain mobile drilling platform, able to sink a well just about anywhere you might need it to go. 

The model is a little bit elaborate. The default parts are divided to make printing less of a headache. The original .3mf file is included in case you feel the need to split it up further. (Microsoft 3D builder is a decent part splitter and is free).

This mech is modeled from real drilling platforms, with pipe handling arms, a rather large top drive, iron roughneck, and so forth. The big cylinder in the back is the pipe rack, intended to be reloaded from the back or just swapped for another full cylinder. Just remember - don't shoot the active drilling rig, you have no idea what it's sitting on!

Also included is a 'waterline' model for those rigs deployed in shallow water areas.

A classy Chinese restaurant to add to your city, this building is designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support placing units on top in all hexes for playability. It is 1 level tall if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

There are four files. One has the building on hexes, another is hexless so that you can print the one that fits your playstyle, and there are two more versions that have the text removed from the front of the building. Using the NoText versions, you can paint custom names on the front, print off logos to attach, or leave it blank.

As always, tipping is appreciated at: paypal.me/rainingfire416

**Notable features:**
-Detailed design including doors, windows, and a detailed roof with greebles.
-Asian-inspired font used for the store name.
-Large yin-yang logo made and placed on the front of the restaurant.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.

The Krumpin' Mega Bot is a hulking, heavily armored monster! Pistons, welded to powerful close combat weapons, such as the Ripper Klaw deliver enormous hydraulik power to every git or vehicle gettin' to close.
Other than the more commonly Deff Bots and or Kans, Krumpin' Mega Bots are usually armed with high speed rattling weapons of high calibers to kill enemies even before reaching them in close combat! (Or just to make horrible loud noise...)

EDIT: Most Parts are compatible to my Skrappin' Mega Bot
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/skrappin-mega-bot
Build your Bot as you like! :-)

FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

This is my ambitious model until now!

To print this monster, you need time or a resin printer ;-)
I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075 or better for all parts to get the quality I intended, while designing this model - please see the pics, those are printed in FDM

(<=0,075mm)!

I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I highly recommend it to use tree supports - make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 for optimal removal

(keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 to 0.075(!) )

For the Rippa Klaw I added a resin version with "_Resin" in the file name - unlike the FDM versions those don't have a flat bottom. (I have not test printed these files, but they

should be good to go!)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
---------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: ----------
----------------------------------------------------------------------


---------- GUN ARM: ----------

THE RATTLA KANNON MAGAZINE IS ROTATABLE IF DONE AS INTENDED!!

For the axies you simply insert usual filament!
If you don't glue the "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_06.stl" to "...05.stl" the "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag.stl" is interchangeable - who knows what might be released in future...... ;-)
-> If you don't want this or don't have filament, just glue the parts as wanted.


Assembly as followed: (please see also the last two pics/screenshots!

1. Stick (NOT glue, if you want it to be removable) together:
"MegaBot_RattlerKannon_05" & "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_06", OPTIONAL: "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Barrel.stl"

2. Insert a 1.75mm filament (42mm long - as the answer to all questions, lol) into "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back_Spacer.stl", large side first, followed by

"MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag".

2.a) Glue on all parts of "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back.stl", if you want more realistic details (even if Ork xD).
2.a.note: Warning: print "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back.stl" with "brim" 3mm+.
They will, regardless of brim width, fall apart after removing the brim. This is intended so you can glue them bitz more random on the Mag!

3. "Dry fit" (NO glue at first!) all parts

3.a) View the last two pics (Tinkercad screenshots)!

3.b) "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Trigger.stl" to
 "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back_Spacer.stl"

3.c) I recommend to glue in "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_TriggerPin.stl" to "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Trigger.stl" first.

3.d) Glue the filament between "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Trigger.stl" & "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back_Spacer.stl"


---------- MAIN BODY ----------

You CAN use two 10x4mm Neodym magnets for the junction "hip <> main hull" to get a rotatable/removable body!

---------- LEGS ----------

The legs are unique, there is a individual model for right / left leg. Those are mirrorable / interchangeable.

---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------

Many parts have a "flat surface" - face those to the build plate.


---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for some coins for coffein I need doin' stuff like that :-D ;-)

Please consider a tip ....this HIGH detailed model was a work of 100h+ of free time (~50 RL days)! If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-) :-):-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

Demon beasts for warmaster both with and without supports using ADeco's awesome minotaur demon. I fattened its lower legs up a bit to keep them from breaking.

10mm demon army
See my collections for the other units; I have a unit for each of the roles in warmaster revolution and a couple of heroes. Note that this army does not inherently match one of the big four chaos gods by design, as I find them dreadfully boring.

Supports
The supports are auto generated by Prusa. To my surprise none of its horns broke off when removing supports, although you should try to be gentle.

Why?
I just got a 3d printer and was looking to get into warmaster with some friends when I noticed that there is no ready to print demon army yet. Given my 0-level modelling skills I instead decided to use existing models to create the army; this unit is one of the outcomes of this project.

Disclaimer
To be sure: none of these models are actually mine. I am a complete hack blundering his way through blender; all I can do is resize models, fatten segments and add cylinders (you may spot some of my handiwork on other models, or here!).

Why?
I just got a 3d printer and was looking to get into warmaster with some friends when I noticed that there is no ready to print demon army yet. Given my 0-level modelling skills I instead decided to use existing models to create the army; this unit is one of the outcomes of this project.

Disclaimer
To be sure: none of these models are actually mine. I am a complete hack blundering his way through blender; all I can do is resize models, fatten segments and add cylinders (you may spot some of my handiwork on other models, or here!).

Thank you to MoonJam and Lord_Arner for many of the base parts!

Some Power Armoured Grey Knights for your Epic needs. These are scaled as 8mm marines like all of Moonjam's stuff. There are all the options needed for the current NetEA Developmental GK list. Everything for Strike Squads, Purgation Squads, Purifier Squads, Interceptor Squads, and even a little Crowe for good measure.

I have included supported .lys files for those who don't want the hassle of supporting them yourself. The supports are way more janky and not as nice as MoonJam's, but they do print. I have test printed them and they work.

Just a note, the painted models in the preview are from a previous version before purity seals were added. May the Emperor have mercy on your eyes when you are painting these.

These are largely based off of MoonJam's amazing Galactic Crusaders. I also took the helmets from Lord_Arner's Daybreak Strikers. There is also a Plaguebearer head for which I cannot find the link from jimjimjimmyjim in there so thanks to him as well. A few bits were my own design but the credit should really be theirs. Thingiverse is dumb and not letting me put their models in the remix section so links to models used are below.

This is my design remix to properly make the most of those soda or beer can you drink while painting or playing warhammer40k. Give them a new life and make they look really cool in your game table.

This pack includes only the pieces to build the preview:

- 2 bottom supports and rings
- front imperial hatch
- back ventilation grille
- side control panel
- side pipe to the ground
- top ventilation fan
- top human access hatch and the ladder to get there

v2 (2021-04-11):

- Added parts needed to build a vertical container with a 330ml slim can. Only needs 2 beds to print in less than 4 hours.

v2.2 (2021-06-20):

- Added Adeptus Mechanicus symbol to 330ml slim version (also can be used as top part in the regular version). Thanks to @Turtlebot for the suggestion.

Also includes the pre-assembled project files for popular slider softwares. 3 beds for short-printing times and get a tank ready in a single day.

All credit goes to:

- Tijnemanske (for his amazing "soda can terrain" design. Search him in thingiverse)

Tired of seeing the enemy aircrafts hunting your troops unchallenged?? We have the solution.
Afraid of enemy long range units shooting down your BTS?? We have the solution.
Worried about that big hordes running towards you?? Yes, WE HAVE THE SOLUTION.

Here you can find 3 wonderful "solutions": anti air tank, missile launcher tank and mortar tank (note that this one is modelled after the newest version, not the classic one).

They all share the same chasis thanks to STC magic and the same turret thanks to MkHand Industries amazing work. Simply print one chasis, one turret and a pair of mirrored weapon options for the tanks you desire, or mix and match then for fun results xD.

As always, I included both supported and unsupported versions.

This is a remix with the following parts:
Track guards: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3647995
Skull insignia: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:399182
Body, turret and weapons by MkHand Industries: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/epic-scale-anti-air-artillery

UPDATE: Added a ZIP with all files in case Thingiverse does its magic again...
Apparently clicking the download all button leads to the 404 page, simply go to thing files tab and download the zip file, simple workaround for a buggy site.

UPDATE: Test printed nicely, except for the missiles that printed kind of weird, I resupported them and reuploaded the fixed files (also updated the ZIP file).

UPDATE 15/Dec/2020: The antiair cannons were too long for my like, so I added 2 more versions closer to the 40k model proportion, so now you can choose xD (also updated the ZIP file).

UPDATE 15/01/2021: Added options with 0 and 1 missiles left (so you can have all possible configurations)

A full infatry company for Epic games.

70 models, not a single repeated pose (although several are very similar xD).
It includes 6 infantry squads (1 with commissar), a company commander squad and a suppreme commander squad.
I used missile launchers instead of autocannons because I find them more dinamic for infantry on the move, I will use autocannons for the heavy weapon teams in the near future.

I have included the chitubox files in case you want to find the unsupported versions of the models.

This is a remix, but Thingiverse keeps failing to allow me link them properly, so here they are:

Infantry models: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3746245
Missile launcher: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3782889
Missile launcher and commissar insignia: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:399182
Chainswords, swords and boltpistols: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4277183
Commissar body: I do not remember where I downloaded it from. If you are the author, please ping me to give you credit.


UPDATE 2020/10/26: Test printed. Everything went perfectly.

UPDATE 2021/01/19: Files replaced for newer versions (Comissar moved to its own thing and 1 pose repeated to replace him, sorry for that!). Same poses but some reduction on support material and HUGE reduction in file size. Added a rar file with all the separate poses both supported and unsupported.

Call it IFV, APC or just mobile cover, this little fellow helps your cannon fodder to get closer to the enemy so they can die faster. Have fun!

Included 3 chasis (standard one, standard one with rear aquila and command one) but only 1 turret.

This is a remix but, again, Thingiverse doesn´t allow me to link them properly, here are the part lists:

Chasis: By Mkhand Forgeworld
Multilaser: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3049352
Track guards: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3647995
Skull insignia: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:399182
Aquila: http://www.thingiverse.com/thing:1363920
Radar: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3753633

UPDATE 26/10/2020: Test printed. They print fine but I broke one of the lasguns from the array on the clean up process and ended up hating the hollowed part (a pain to clean). I will soon upload new models with tougher lasgun arrays and radar receptor, as well as more pronounced aquilas for the command body (they are barely visible).

UPDATE 28/10/2020: Added second versions for standard and command body, as promised. Also included a second version of the turret, it just has a bigger peg.
If you are upscaling the models, consider using the first ones, they are more accurate.
Test printed at 0.04 and 0.02, both went great.

This is a Curtiss-Wright J2 Fury from the game Crimson Skies. **This version is bigger than game pieces and has a little more detail, the idea is to print it to be used as desktop token just for Crimson Skies fans**

**Remember you can leave a tip for the zeppelin crew here: [Beer for the crew](https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/toposolitario)**

Creating Crimson Skies planes for 3D printing is something that no-one has done previously. And it is a shame as the planes are pretty iconic and after many years from it discreet publishing, FASA's Crimson Skies still has a lot of fans who play or are willing to play from time to time.

I started this for testing the VR modelling tool Gravity Sketch, and I found that work flow is so quick that a new plane can be created from zero in almost an hour. First I made the Fury (the one I like most), and the results for it and the Peacemaker were so good that I finally am willing to complete the full series (basic box plus the Balmoral).

In the end... I'll have a good bunch of pieces just to frankenbuild almost any flying perversion just by dragging and dropping! XD

It is not designed to be printer friendly, but it is coming out perfect with resin printers and pretty good in FDM (I suggest to print them vertically with supports growing from the tail).

*Honk if you're a Crimson Skies fan!!*

In the 31st century, this originally Canadian business has rebranded to be even more popular! This building is designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support placing units on top for playability. It is 2 levels tall on the higher levels and 1 level tall on the lower levels if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

This is a two part print. Part 1 of the building can be used standalone as any large commercial building if you print the version without text and a logo. Part 2 is an automotive center add-on that can be placed on either side of the main building to make it larger, as seen in the photos above.

There are six files. Two have the building sections on hexes, two are hexless so that you can print the ones that fits your playstyle, and there are two more versions of Part 1 that have the text removed from the front of the building. Using the NoText versions, you can populate your tabletop with custom commercial/big-box stores by painting names on the front or printing off logos to attach.

As always, tipping is appreciated at: paypal.me/rainingfire416

Notable features:
-Based off of a very popular Canadian business, using a similar font and building design style.
-Detailed design including large front windows, two main entrances, garage doors, windows, and bollards to protect the building from bad drivers.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.
